implementation_notes: resilience4j's Retry module wraps the callable instead of the call site: build a RetryConfig (maxAttempts defaults to 3, waitDuration to 500ms, plus retryExceptions/ignoreExceptions and a retryOnResultPredicate) or take a named Retry from a RetryRegistry, then decorate the Supplier, Callable or CompletionStage with Retry.decorate* - the decorator re-invokes the operation, applies the wait and throws MaxRetriesExceededException (or rethrows the last failure) when the budget is spent. IntervalFunction.ofExponentialBackoff() and ofRandomized() replace the fixed wait without touching the decorated code, which is the reason to use the library rather than a loop: the policy becomes a configuration object shared by name across the application. A hand-written loop with Thread.sleep remains justified in a dependency-free library, but not in a service that already uses resilience4j for circuit breaking.
pitfalls: retryExceptions and ignoreExceptions are type-based only: a business failure that extends a retryable exception class is retried unless it is listed in ignoreExceptions, so the taxonomy must be explicit.
maxAttempts counts the initial call as the first attempt (maxAttempts(2) means one retry), the opposite convention from most retry libraries.
The Retry instance is thread-safe, but the decorated call's Try/result must stay per invocation; sharing it across threads mixes attempt state.
Waiting happens on the calling thread (or the completion thread for CompletionStage decoration): a synchronous retry consumes a request-handling thread for the whole delay.
When retry and circuit breaker are combined, decide the order deliberately: retrying outside an open breaker multiplies calls that the breaker would have rejected.

variants.name: MicroProfile Fault Tolerance @Retry on a CDI bean method
variants.idiom_name: @Retry(maxRetries = 2) interceptor with config overrides via MicroProfile Config
variants.implementation_notes: MicroProfile Fault Tolerance moves the policy into an annotation: @Retry(maxRetries = 2) on a CDI bean method makes the container interceptor re-invoke the method, and the parameters can be overridden at deployment time through MicroProfile Config (Retry/maxRetries=6 globally, or <class>/<method>/Retry/maxRetries per method) - the point of the declarative form being that the attempt budget becomes configuration rather than code. The same annotation set composes retry with timeout, bulkhead, circuit breaker and fallback (@Fallback(fallbackMethod = ...)), so the failure path is visible in the method signature. Choose it in Jakarta EE/MicroProfile applications where interception is available; the programmatic decorator is the alternative elsewhere.
pitfalls: maxRetries counts additional attempts after the first call, so maxRetries = 2 means three executions in total - the opposite convention from resilience4j's maxAttempts.
Annotations only take effect through an interceptor: self-invocation inside the same bean, or a call on a non-CDI object, bypasses the retry entirely.
There is no backoff parameter in the annotation: pacing comes from the underlying call's timeout, and retrying a non-idempotent method duplicates its effect.
The interceptor re-invokes the whole method, so local state mutated before the failure is re-executed too - keep the method side-effect-free up to the call being retried.
